ledger.note: October 1360: King John II creates the duchy of Berry as an appanage for his third son John of Poitiers. Page: 'On October 1360, King John II created the peerage-duchy of Berry as an appanage for his third-born son'; infobox capital Bourges.

1360: Auvergne is raised to a duchy for John with Berry. 'When Poitiers was ceded to England in 1360, his father granted John the newly raised duchies of Berry and Auvergne'; the Crown lands page lists 'Poitiers, Mâcon, Angoulême, Auvergne' with the Berry appanage.

1378: the French reconquer the lands lost at Brétigny, among them Poitou, of which John was count. Hundred Years' War page: 'By 1378 ... the French had reconquered most of the lands ceded to King Edward in the Treaty of Brétigny'; John of Berry page: 'In 1356, he was made Count of Poitou by his father' (infobox 1357-1416), while Poitiers had been ceded to England in 1360. The pages do not say on which date Poitou came into John's hands in fact.
15 June 1416: John of Berry dies and Poitou merges into the royal domain. Page: 'John died on 15 June 1416 in Paris'; infobox: Poitou vacant and merged into the royal domain.

1416: Auvergne goes to John's daughter Marie. Page: Marie 'succeeded him as Duchess of Auvergne'. Marie 'married first Louis III of Châtillon, then Philip of Artois, Count of Eu and finally John I, Duke of Bourbon' (same page); the house-of-bourbon dossier carries the 1416 Auvergne gain and royal-domain-of-france takes Auvergne from house-of-bourbon in 1531. [Reviewer eu-10-x, 2026-10-25] counterpart changed from county-of-auvergne, a different polity (the comital Auvergne).

1416: Berry passes to John's grandnephew Dauphin John and, in 1417, to Dauphin Charles. Page: 'Upon his death in 1416, John of Poitiers was succeeded as Duke of Berry by his grandnephew'; 'When the Dauphin ascended to the throne as Charles VII, Berry returned to the royal domain.' The Crown lands page says 'Berry returns' in 1416.

wars.note: John of Berry was a hostage of the English crown until 1369 (John of Berry page) and was lieutenant general in Languedoc 1380-1388; neither is territory.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from four pages (Duchy of Berry, John Duke of Berry, Crown lands of France, Hundred Years' War). The Duchy of Berry page is the article on the title, not on the territory; it gives no area. This dossier is John of Berry's composite (Berry, Auvergne, Poitou), 1360-1416; the later Berry apanages (Charles of France 1461-1472, Joan of France 1498, Marguerite 1527, Margaret of Valois 1550, Francis of Anjou 1576-1584, the 1778 recreation) are not drawn and the page gives no territory for them.
DISAGREEMENTS: John was Count of Poitou from 1356 (text) or 1357 (infobox); the Crown lands page puts Poitiers, Mâcon and Angoulême in the 1360 row though Poitiers was ceded to England in 1360 (John page); the Duchy page says Berry passed to Dauphin John in 1416 and returned to the royal domain with Charles VII, the Crown lands page says 'Berry returns' in 1416 (the royal-domain-of-france dossier draws it as domain from 1416). Mâcon and Angoulême (c. 1372-1374) are not drawn: no region and no dates. Languedoc was an office (1380-1388), not land.
CONSISTENCY: royal-domain-of-france loses Berry and Auvergne in 1360 to this dossier and gets Berry and Poitou back in 1416.
